correctness.rationale: A random oriented cyclic triangle has angles (A,B,C) with (A,B) uniform density 2/π² on A>0,B>0,A+B<π, by the Dirichlet(1,1,1) boundary-gap law. With x=cot A,y=cot B,z=cot C, identity xy+yz+zx=1 and K=x+y+z yield an exact radius-s cotangent circle s²=K²−3. The parametrization x=(K+2s cos φ)/3, y=(K+2s cos(φ+2π/3))/3, z=(K+2s cos(φ+4π/3))/3 bijects the positive-angle simplex except its equilateral point. Its two-dimensional Jacobian |∂(x,y)/∂(K,φ)|=(x+y)/√3 gives |∂(A,B)/∂(K,φ)|=9√3/[2(K³+9K−s³ cos3φ)]. Multiplying 2/π² gives the joint density. Direct algebra verifies (K³+9K)²−(K²−3)³=27(1+K²)²; integrating 1/(a−b cos 3φ) gives f_K=6/[π(1+K²)]. Since dK/domega=−(1+K²), omega is uniform on (0,π/6). Normalized conditional kernel has r=b/(a+√(a²−b²)) and its weak limits r→0 and 1. Density tail ~k^-2 establishes moments p<1. Independent centered finite-difference Jacobians at (K,φ)=(2.1,0.1),(4,1.3),(10,2.5) agreed with exact Jacobian within ~10^−9 relative; this corroborates, but the distribution proof is analytic.

value.rationale: An exact, unexpectedly uniform nonlinear geometric angle law for the simplest natural random cyclic triangle, plus the full correlated marked shape distribution, supplies reusable closed-form sampling and conditional law beyond textbook cotangent identities. The exact first-moment and moment cutoff are natural consequences; the substantive value is the evaluated joint probability law, not numerical simulation.

final_claim: For three independent arclength-uniform points on a circle, the geometric Brocard angle omega is exactly Uniform(0,π/6), equivalent to f_K(k)=6/[π(1+k²)] for K=cot omega>√3. For the cyclically ordered triangle the cotangent-circle phase has exact joint density 9√3/{π²[k³+9k−(k²−3)^(3/2)cos(3φ)]}, whose conditional phase is a threefold wrapped Poisson kernel; tails and moment cutoff follow.
limitations: Only iid arclength-uniform circle points; the phase depends on cyclic labels and is undefined at the probability-zero equilateral case.
No claims for disk-uniform or Gaussian triangles; an unindexed classical Brocard-law identity remains possible.
residual_risks: An equivalent classical marginal may be catalogued under triangle shape statistics or a transformed cone angle without Brocard in the title.

The hyperbolic ideal incenter threefold Poisson law uses the same random sample and bears a close structural resemblance; equality after an undiscovered deterministic transformation cannot be excluded, though no direct same-variable implication was established.
